summary.text: Republican Scott Petersen won the election for Nebraska Secretary of State on November 3, 2026, defeating Sarah Slattery, according to unofficial results, and is set to take office when the new term begins.
An Omaha business owner and former Douglas County Republican Party chairman, he defeated incumbent Bob Evnen in the May 2026 primary.

paragraphs.text: Petersen earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Iowa in 1976.
He describes himself as a Nebraska business owner and conservative leader with more than 30 years of experience building and operating businesses in the state.

Petersen served as chairman of the Douglas County Republican Party and sits on the Nebraska Republican Party's State Executive Committee, and he was a delegate to the 2024 Republican National Convention.
In 2020 he was the Republican candidate for Douglas County Clerk-Comptroller and lost to incumbent Daniel Esch, a Democrat, with 45.8% of the vote.
He has never held elected office.
Petersen challenged Evnen from the right and won the May 12, 2026 Republican primary with 54.6% of the vote to Evnen's 45.4%.
He said his priorities were secure, transparent and accountable elections, and that he would bring a business-minded approach to the office's business services and public records work.
During the campaign, he emphasized restoring confidence in elections through accurate voter rolls, chain-of-custody procedures and transparency.

He won the November 3, 2026 general election for Secretary of State of Nebraska with 53.7% of the vote to Sarah Slattery's 40.6% and Paul Rumbaugh's 3.1% and 1 other candidate, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
